row.title: Apply the statutory definitions of unexpected, suspected and serious ADR when recording and reporting ADRs
row.statement: When recording and reporting suspected adverse reactions (Arts 194b-194c), the MAH must apply the statutory definitions: 'unexpected' (not in the SmPC, or nature, severity or outcome not consistent with it), 'suspected' (reporter or MAH assumes a possible causal relationship) and 'serious' (causing death, immediate danger to life, hospitalisation or its prolongation, significant or lasting damage, disability or congenital anomaly).

row.quote_en: h) Communicate to the Directorate of Medicines and Health Technology and to the Clinical Research Ethics Committee involved in the study: 1. All serious and unexpected adverse reactions that may be related to the investigational treatments, occurring inside or outside the country. 2. Any information derived from studies in animals suggesting a significant risk for human beings, including any finding of teratogenicity or carcinogenicity. The sponsor together with the investigator shall take the necessary measures to protect the study subjects.
